Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

national adjective

of a whole country or people

also nationwide, national holiday, national language, national team, national costume, national debt

classical

Caes. BG 6.13.4: sacrificia pūblica ac prīvāta
M-O s.v. national debt: dēbitum pūblicum

pūblicus, pūblica, pūblicum

adjective

of the state or the whole people: national, as against private or local

Latin says “national” with the state’s own words: pūblicus for what belongs to the whole state, and the people’s own adjective (Rōmānus, Graecus) for what belongs to one nation.

Other words

  • patrius, patria, patrium — of one’s own country, native: national (language, customs, songs)

    adjective · also used · classical · Curt. 3.3.9: Magī proximī patrium carmen canēbant; Cic. Fin. 1.4: patrius sermō (Lewis & Short)

    Lewis & Short translate Curtius’s patrium carmen “a national song”.

  • nostrās, nostrātis — of our country, home-grown

    adjective, third declension, one ending · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 9.15.2: facētiīs, maximē nostrātibus (Lewis & Short)

    Cicero’s word for what is our own: verba nostrātia, home-grown words (Fam. 2.11.1, Lewis & Short).

  • genticus, gentica, genticum — national, of a people

    adjective · also used · classical · Tac. Ann. 3.43: mōre genticō (Lewis & Short)

    Rare and post-Augustan: Tacitus, of a people’s own custom.

  • nātiōnālis, nātiōnāle — national

    adjective, third declension · also used · modern · M-O s.v. nation-state: cīvitās nātiōnālis

    Not ancient: classical nātiō is a people or a tribe, and has no adjective.

Examples

  • Illī rēbus dīvīnīs intersunt, sacrificia pūblica ac prīvāta prōcūrant, religiōnēs interpretantur

    They take part in worship, look after the sacrifices of the state and of private people, and interpret religious questionsCaes. BG 6.13.4

  • Magī proximī patrium carmen canēbant

    Next came the Magi, singing their national hymnCurt. 3.3.9

See also state, international, foreign, people, language.

SourcesLewis & Short: publicus · Lewis & Short: patrius · Lewis & Short: nostras · Lewis & Short: genticus · Lewis & Short: natio
